notes: The letter voices retributive judgment in images of affliction, fire and lasting destruction; the violence is retained as the author’s claim.
The pinned text says ‘day of the Lord.’
The pinned text reads ‘man of lawlessness’; manuscripts also preserve a ‘sin’ reading.
The text does not identify either the restraining power or the one who restrains.
The pinned reading is ‘firstfruits’; another early reading can mean ‘from the beginning.’
vocabulary: Be present or have arrived; the claim denied here is that the day is already present.

notes: The condition concerns someone unwilling to work, not a person unable to work.
The social boundary is expressly limited: the person is to be warned as family, not treated as an enemy.
